analysis.title: GS Basics - Land & Power. 2027 vs 2029. Vol Compression
key_insights: Equity futures dipped sharply overnight after legislative margins and key regional races were decided, then recovered meaningfully. The author suspects vol will struggle to sustain a bid and the initial selloff will be absorbed.
Many hedges were put on in recent days and now need to be monetized. Multiples have already de-rated aggressively, especially in AI infrastructure.

The AI debate has shifted from the cost of compute to whether capacity can be permitted, energized and delivered in 2027-2029. Moratoriums, local opposition to data centers and a more restrictive regulatory environment could constrain supply.

For sellers of chips, cooling, electrical equipment and data center components, customers may have overordered relative to the capacity they can energize. Some demand could move to other geographies or behind-the-meter power, but not quickly enough. Much of this risk appears reflected in multiples.
If new supply cannot be delivered, the scarcity value of existing energized compute should rise. This potentially benefits hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity.

Neoclouds differ: some have substantial existing compute and contracted demand, others depend on new facilities, financing and power delivery. Owning compute today versus promising compute tomorrow is the key distinction.
Throttling compute supply does not necessarily destroy demand and could push pricing higher for longer.

Policy uncertainty over corporate tax rates, antitrust/M&A and administrative oversight after 2028 can cap terminal multiples. The counterargument is that with current administration leadership in place through 2028, companies have an incentive to pull forward capital deployment, permitting and transactions into 2027.
The S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterm election cycles since 1950.

Geopolitics is unresolved: mediators are exchanging proposals, a limited deal is possible but the sides remain far apart. Trilateral Russia/Ukraine/US talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11.
AMD reported revenue +45% YoY to $13.4bn and data center +97% to $8.5bn, with Q4 guidance implying another 27% sequential acceleration. Both EPYC CPU demand and Instinct GPU ramp are contributing.
Intel's data center business grew 78% YoY, so the author reads Intel's weak print as a supply/execution and profitability story, not a demand warning.
The author finds it hard to reconcile AMD's accelerating growth with the scale of multiple compression across the AI complex.

Bottom line: AI infrastructure has been 'sold to death', the micro is strong, electoral uncertainty has diminished and positioning looks cleaner. Vol likely comes in quickly and that drives spot in the short term.

tension_points.bull_case: Constrained supply of compute raises the scarcity value of existing energized compute, benefiting hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity, and could push pricing higher for longer. Multiples have already de-rated and AMD's growth is accelerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Moratoriums, local opposition and regulation may stop customers from energizing the capacity they ordered, a risk for chip, cooling and electrical equipment suppliers. Neoclouds dependent on new facilities, financing and power are exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Geopolitical escalation, which the desk calls the swing factor, or vol failing to come in with many hedges still outstanding.

tension_points.bull_case: With current administration leadership through 2028, companies have an incentive to pull forward capital deployment, permitting and transactions into 2027, and the market may look past 2029 policy changes.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty over future corporate tax rates, antitrust/M&A and administrative oversight can cap terminal multiples.
